result.summary: Block on unbounded batch memory and inconsistent quota validation. All five tests pass despite both defects. Issue #90 could not be fetched.

findings.title: Batching materializes the entire input and output
findings.body: list(records) exhausts the iterable, then the comprehension retains every batch simultaneously. A tracemalloc probe with 10 million repeated None records peaked at 162,424,336 bytes, contradicting the documented under-4-MB claim even without allocating record payloads. Large inputs can exhaust memory before any batch reaches the caller.
findings.recommendation: Yield batches incrementally from an iterator using islice. Test that obtaining the first batch consumes only one batch of input and that memory remains bounded as input size grows.

findings.title: Equivalent quota allocations receive different verdicts
findings.body: The raw floating-point comparison rejects [0.9] but accepts [0.3, 0.3, 0.3], although both allocate 90%. Their computed reserves fall on opposite sides of 0.1 because of rounding. The new equal-shares test enshrines this accidental acceptance, so regrouping the same allocation can change whether validation succeeds.
findings.recommendation: Define whether exactly 10% reserve is allowed and enforce that policy with decimal or integer quota units. Test equivalent partitions and allocations immediately above and below the boundary.

next_steps: Implement bounded-memory iteration and deterministic quota boundary handling, then add regression tests for the reproduced failures.
